draft: Field try drafts for editors (idea engine, 24 Oct 2026). Spec 21 Part B. Not fact-checked by an editor.

oldQuest.title: Spot a small step
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up training log, mark the first clean rise in reps or load.

fieldTry.title: Progressive overload
fieldTry.detail: Count how many times you carry a bag up stairs today; add no extra trips.
fieldTry.smaller: Notice one bag you already carry today.
settings: With a bag you carry daily
fieldTry.notice: Strength grows when the load, the reps or the days go up bit by bit.

noticeClaim.text: Strength grows over time when the weight, the sets or reps, or the days a week of training go up bit by bit.

oldQuest.title: Name the three parts
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up gym day, mark the work, the food and the time away from hard work.

fieldTry.title: Muscle, protein and rest
fieldTry.detail: At one meal today, name the food on your plate that carries protein.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one protein food you ate today.
fieldTry.notice: Most people who train can get enough protein from food alone, without powders.

noticeClaim.text: Most people who train can get enough protein from food alone, without powders. People with kidney disease should take care with high protein.

oldQuest.title: Read a training story
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up exam week, mark the sleep gap and the later match and hunger clues.

fieldTry.title: Sleep and recovery
fieldTry.detail: This morning, note when you put the phone down last night and when you woke.
fieldTry.smaller: Note when you woke this morning.
settings: Before a match or exam day
fieldTry.notice: Experts advise adults to sleep 7 to 9 hours a night.

noticeClaim.text: Experts advise adults to sleep 7 to 9 hours a night.

oldQuest.title: Read the hot-day switch
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up Train screen, mark which changes cut heat strain and which add it.

fieldTry.title: Heat and hydration
fieldTry.detail: Check today's hottest hours in a weather app, and when it is cooler.
fieldTry.smaller: Check today's top temperature.
cues: When I plan a walk or game
fieldTry.notice: In hot weather, training early or late, when it is cooler, and starting slow cut heat strain.

noticeClaim.text: In hot weather, train early or late when it is cooler, start slow and pick up the pace bit by bit, and drink more water than usual without waiting for thirst.

oldQuest.title: Spot the easy start
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up cricket warm-up, mark when the work first moves from easy to hard.

fieldTry.title: Warm-up and injury myths
fieldTry.detail: Watch people at a ground, park or gym, and spot the easy start.
fieldTry.smaller: Recall how your last game began: easy or hard?
fieldTry.notice: A warm-up is usually the activity done slower or lighter, so heart rate and breathing rise bit by bit.

noticeClaim.text: A warm-up is usually the activity done at a slower speed or lower effort, such as brisk walking before jogging, so heart rate and breathing rise bit by bit. A cool-down does the same at the end.

oldQuest.title: Sort the talk clues
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up walk, ride and run, mark where speech is easy, short or in between.

fieldTry.title: Cardio zones and talk test
fieldTry.detail: On a walk you already take, silently note if you could say a full sentence.
fieldTry.smaller: After stairs you already take, notice your breath.
settings: A brisk walk with a friend
fieldTry.notice: At moderate effort you can talk but not sing; at vigorous effort only a few words come out.

noticeClaim.text: As a rule of thumb, at moderate effort you can talk but not sing; at vigorous effort you cannot say more than a few words without pausing for breath.

oldQuest.title: Find the repeat
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up week, mark the small sessions tied to the same daily cue.

fieldTry.title: Habit of showing up
fieldTry.detail: After one daily act, notice if a short walk or stairs already follows it.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one daily act that a walk already follows.
fieldTry.notice: Brisk bouts of any length count, so even a few flights of stairs counts.

noticeClaim.text: Brisk bouts of any length count. The old rule of at least 10 minutes was dropped, so even a few flights of stairs counts.

oldQuest.title: Compare two mock packs
oldQuest.detail: Read the added sugars, the stressed ingredient's % and the %RDA on two made-up labels.

fieldTry.title: Food labels in India
fieldTry.detail: Pick up one pack at home and find its added sugars line.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the ingredients list on one pack.
fieldTry.notice: Labels show total sugars and added sugars as separate lines; added sugars are only the sugars put in.

noticeClaim.text: Labels show total sugars and added sugars as separate lines; added sugars are only the sugars put into the food.

oldQuest.title: Spot the protein
oldQuest.detail: Look at one meal and name its protein foods, such as dal, milk, eggs or nuts.

fieldTry.title: Protein in everyday food
fieldTry.detail: At one meal today, note if it has a cereal, millet or pulse. None counts too.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one protein food at one meal.
settings: At a wedding or party meal
fieldTry.notice: Cereals or millets and pulses can fill gaps in each other's amino acid mix.

noticeClaim.text: Cereals or millets and pulses can fill gaps in each other’s amino acid mix.

oldQuest.title: Read a drink label
oldQuest.detail: Find a drink label and note its sugar entry. Ask whether sugar was added or came from juice.

fieldTry.title: Free sugars
fieldTry.detail: Read the sugar line on one drink you see today.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the word sugar in one ingredients list.
fieldTry.notice: One can of sugar-sweetened soda can hold up to 40 g of free sugars, about 10 teaspoons.

noticeClaim.text: One can of sugar-sweetened soda can hold up to 40 g of free sugars, about 10 teaspoons, and a tablespoon of ketchup about 4 g.

oldQuest.title: Notice fluids
oldQuest.detail: For one day, note the drinks you have, tea and milk included, with no target to meet.

fieldTry.title: Hydration cues
fieldTry.detail: Today, count your drinks, tea and milk included. There is no target.
fieldTry.smaller: Count your drinks from morning to lunch.
settings: On a busy college or work day
fieldTry.notice: Water, lower-fat milk and lower-sugar drinks, including tea and coffee, all count towards daily fluid.

noticeClaim.text: Water, lower-fat milk and lower-sugar drinks, including tea and coffee, all count towards daily fluid.

oldQuest.title: Pick a wake time
oldQuest.detail: Choose one wake time for the next three days and notice how falling asleep feels.

fieldTry.title: Sleep and recovery
fieldTry.detail: Today, note if you woke near your usual time. Set no new wake time.
fieldTry.smaller: Note when you woke this morning.
fieldTry.notice: The same bed and wake time each day is one of the habits that help sleep.

noticeClaim.text: Habits that help sleep include the same bed and wake time each day, a quiet, cool and dark bedroom, devices off at least 30 minutes before bed, and no caffeine late in the day.

oldQuest.title: Feel a pulse change
oldQuest.detail: Notice your pulse and breathing at rest and after an easy walk. Treat it as a change to observe, not a score.

fieldTry.title: Exercise and the heart
fieldTry.detail: Count your brisk minutes today, walks and stairs included.
fieldTry.smaller: Count the brisk minutes of one walk.
cues: On my way to class or work
fieldTry.notice: Activity can be spread through the week in smaller chunks, and some is better than none.

noticeClaim.text: Activity can be spread through the week in smaller chunks, and some is better than none.

oldQuest.title: Find a vitamin C helper
oldQuest.detail: Look at one meal with dal or greens and name a vitamin C food that could go with it.

fieldTry.title: Iron and anaemia basics
fieldTry.detail: At a meal with dal or greens, spot a vitamin C food, like lemon or guava.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one vitamin C food in your kitchen.
fieldTry.notice: Vitamin C foods like guava, oranges or lemon help the body take in iron from plant foods.

noticeClaim.text: Vitamin C foods like guava, oranges or lemon help the body take in iron from plant foods, while tea and coffee get in the way.

oldQuest.title: Compare two labels
oldQuest.detail: Look at two similar packs and find the same per-100 g or per-100 ml line on each.

fieldTry.title: Reading a food label
fieldTry.detail: Compare two similar packs on the same per-100 g or per-100 ml line.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the per-100 g column on one pack.
fieldTry.notice: Values per 100 g or 100 ml let you compare like foods; each brand sets its own serving size.

noticeClaim.text: Nutrition values are given per 100 g or 100 ml, and may also be given per serving, whose size each brand sets.

oldQuest.title: Check a bold food claim
oldQuest.detail: Find a food ad that says one item does everything. Ask which food groups it leaves out.

fieldTry.title: Fad diet claims
fieldTry.detail: Spot one ad that says one food does it all, and name a food group it leaves out.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one superfood claim today.
fieldTry.notice: No one food gives all the key nutrients.

noticeClaim.text: ICMR-NIN says to eat from many food groups. No one food gives all the key nutrients.

oldQuest.title: Trace a water path
oldQuest.detail: On a walk, trace where rain or used water can leave a building and enter a public drain.

fieldTry.title: Indus Valley cities
fieldTry.detail: On a usual walk, spot one drain cover from the footpath. Stay away from openings.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one drain cover from the footpath.
settings: In an old part of town
fieldTry.notice: All the streets and lanes of Mohenjo-daro had drains, most covered with baked bricks.

noticeClaim.text: All the streets and lanes of Mohenjo-daro had drains. Most were covered with baked bricks, and pipes and chutes from houses led into them.

oldQuest.title: Read a public message
oldQuest.detail: Find a public notice and ask whom it can reach beyond the person who wrote it.

fieldTry.title: Ashoka's edicts
fieldTry.detail: Find one public notice and ask who can read it, and who it misses.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one public sign in two languages.
cues: At a bus stop or station
settings: At a temple, mosque or church
fieldTry.notice: Most people in Ashoka's time could probably not read, so officers were sent to spread the message.

noticeClaim.text: Most people then could probably not read. Special officers were sent to spread the message of dhamma.

oldQuest.title: Map an idea
oldQuest.detail: Pick an everyday idea and trace two places or people through whom it reached you.

fieldTry.title: Silk Road ideas
fieldTry.detail: Ask an elder where one food or word you use daily came from.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one everyday thing that came from far away.
fieldTry.notice: Monks who appear to have been forced out of Gandhara took its art style to Afghanistan and Central Asia.

noticeClaim.text: Hun invasions appear to have forced monks from Gandhara into Afghanistan and Central Asia. Their art style then grew popular at Buddhist sites there.

oldQuest.title: Spot an empty place
oldQuest.detail: Write 205 and 25. Point to the place that zero keeps open in the first number.

fieldTry.title: Indian place value and zero
fieldTry.detail: Find one price with a zero inside it, and name the zero's place.
fieldTry.smaller: Find one number with a zero today.
fieldTry.notice: In the Indian base ten system, zero can mark an empty place in a number.

noticeClaim.text: In the Indian base ten system, zero can mark an empty place in a number.

oldQuest.title: Follow one page
oldQuest.detail: Find one shared printed page and ask how many readers may see the same words.

fieldTry.title: Printing and reading
fieldTry.detail: Spot one printed notice put up where many people can see it.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one printed notice today.
settings: At a tea stall with a paper
fieldTry.notice: Printing put knowledge within reach of every person who knew how to read.

noticeClaim.text: Printing put knowledge within reach of every person who knew how to read.

oldQuest.title: Trace a public service
oldQuest.detail: Name one service that needs records and resources to work across many towns.

fieldTry.title: Mughal administration
fieldTry.detail: On one bill or public form, find a date or record number. Keep personal details private.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the date on one receipt you already have.
fieldTry.notice: Mughal zabt worked where officials could survey land and keep careful accounts.

noticeClaim.text: This tax system, zabt, worked where officials could survey land and keep careful accounts. It did not work in provinces such as Gujarat and Bengal.

oldQuest.title: Follow a trade route
oldQuest.detail: Pick an old market or port on a map. Ask what goods moved and who set the rules.

fieldTry.title: Company trade and rule
fieldTry.detail: Find where three things at home were made, from their labels.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the made-in line on one item.
settings: On a phone or charger box
fieldTry.notice: In 1600 the East India Company got a charter giving it the sole English right to trade with the East.

noticeClaim.text: In 1600 the East India Company got a charter from Queen Elizabeth I. It gave the Company the sole English right to trade with the East.

oldQuest.title: Read a shared rule
oldQuest.detail: Find a school or local rule. Ask who made it and who it is meant to serve.

fieldTry.title: Independence and Constitution
fieldTry.detail: Find one rule at college, work or your building, and ask who made it.
fieldTry.smaller: Read one rule on a notice board.
settings: A family rule, on a call home
fieldTry.notice: While debating the draft, the Assembly discussed and decided 2,473 of the 7,635 changes put forward.

noticeClaim.text: While debating the draft, the Assembly discussed and decided 2,473 of the 7,635 changes put forward.

oldQuest.title: Try a paper wing
oldQuest.detail: Fold a paper glider. Watch what happens as it slows. Mark the air flow and the lift path on a sketch.

fieldTry.title: Lift
fieldTry.detail: Fold a paper glider, throw it gently, and watch what happens as it slows.
fieldTry.smaller: Watch a bird or kite glide, and notice when it slows.
settings: A kite on a windy day
fieldTry.notice: Lift needs air moving past a wing; no air or no motion means no lift.

noticeClaim.text: Lift needs air moving past a wing. No air or no motion means no lift, and it does not matter whether the wing or the air is moving.

oldQuest.title: Sketch four motors
oldQuest.detail: Draw a top view of a four-motor craft. Mark which side needs more push for a roll. Label yaw, pitch and roll.

fieldTry.title: How a multirotor turns
fieldTry.detail: Tilt a book once, and point where a push out of its top face would go.
fieldTry.smaller: Tilt a book and point where its top face points.
settings: A wedding with a camera drone
fieldTry.notice: Every pitch or roll aims part of the push sideways, so a tilted drone starts to move.

noticeClaim.text: Every pitch or roll also aims part of the push sideways, so a tilted drone starts to move.

oldQuest.title: Draw an energy trade
oldQuest.detail: Sketch two made-up batteries. Add arrows for more stored energy and more mass. Say how each may change flight time.

fieldTry.title: Batteries and flight time
fieldTry.detail: Note your phone's battery % now and in one hour, and what you used it for.
fieldTry.smaller: Open the battery screen and find the top app.
fieldTry.notice: Flight time depends on stored energy and the rate at which it is used.

noticeClaim.text: Flight time depends on stored energy and the rate at which it is used.

oldQuest.title: Make a sensor map
oldQuest.detail: On paper, draw a drone and link tilt, place and height to the motion sensors, GPS and barometer. Add one limit for each.

fieldTry.title: Flight sensors
fieldTry.detail: Open a map app outdoors, then indoors, and compare the circle round the dot.
fieldTry.smaller: Open your map app indoors and look at the circle.
fieldTry.notice: GPS phones are usually within 4.9 metres under open sky, but buildings and indoor use make it worse.

noticeClaim.text: GPS phones are usually within 4.9 metres under open sky, but buildings, trees and indoor use make it worse.

oldQuest.title: Spot two pushes
oldQuest.detail: Watch a bird and a plane clip. Draw an arrow for forward push and one for lift on each.

fieldTry.title: Why birds flap but planes do not
fieldTry.detail: Watch a bird take off and notice the downstroke.
fieldTry.smaller: Watch one bird flap for 10 seconds.
fieldTry.notice: In small parrots, the downstroke uses nearly all the flapping power, and the upstroke costs almost none.

noticeClaim.text: In small parrots, the downstroke uses nearly all the flapping power, while the upstroke costs almost none.

oldQuest.title: Map a breeze
oldQuest.detail: With the fan on, hold a light ribbon well away from the blades and sketch which way the air flows. Stay on the floor; never climb up to a moving fan.

fieldTry.title: How a ceiling fan moves air
fieldTry.detail: Stand under a fan, then away from it. Is the room cooler, or just you?
fieldTry.smaller: Notice one fan running in an empty room.
fieldTry.notice: Moving air helps sweat dry off your skin, which is mainly how a fan makes you feel cooler.

noticeClaim.text: Moving air helps sweat dry off your skin, which mainly is how a fan makes you feel cooler.

oldQuest.title: Trace a payment
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up canteen payment, label the payer, payee, ID and banks.

fieldTry.title: How UPI moves money
fieldTry.detail: At a shop QR stand, read the printed payee name or UPI ID. No scan, no payment.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one shop QR stand without scanning it.
fieldTry.notice: A UPI ID is a payment address that points to a linked bank account.

noticeClaim.text: A UPI ID is a payment address that you set, and it points to your linked bank account.

oldQuest.title: Trace the light
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up phone diagram, label lens, sensor, colour filters and saved image.

fieldTry.title: How a phone camera takes a photo
fieldTry.detail: Photograph one plain object in bright and dim light. Keep people out.
fieldTry.smaller: Take one dim-light photo of a plain object.
settings: A plain object on a table
fieldTry.notice: A high ISO in dim light gives a bright but grainy photo, because it multiplies the signal.

noticeClaim.text: Turning up ISO multiplies the signal but does not make the sensor more sensitive, so a high ISO in dim light gives a bright but grainy photo.

oldQuest.title: Follow a ray
oldQuest.detail: Draw a short noon path and a longer sunset path through clear air. Never look straight at the Sun.

fieldTry.title: Blue sky and red sunsets
fieldTry.detail: At sunset, look at the sky away from the Sun and name its colours.
fieldTry.smaller: At midday, look away from the Sun and name the sky colour.
fieldTry.notice: At sunset, sunlight takes a longer path through the air, so mostly yellow to red reaches us.

noticeClaim.text: At sunrise and sunset, sunlight takes a longer path through the air, so mostly the yellow-to-red part reaches us.

oldQuest.title: Compare two pots
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up cooking diagram, label the pressure and boiling point in each pot. Mark where to keep hands away from the steam.

fieldTry.title: Pressure cooker
fieldTry.detail: On one cooker meal at home, count the whistles from a safe distance.
fieldTry.smaller: When it is cold, find the weight on your cooker's vent.
fieldTry.notice: A pressure cooker cooks faster because its higher pressure raises the boiling point of the water.

noticeClaim.text: A pressure cooker cooks faster because its higher pressure raises the boiling point of the water inside.

fieldTry.title: Inflation
fieldTry.detail: Ask an elder what one everyday item cost when they were your age.
fieldTry.smaller: Note today's price of one thing you buy often.
fieldTry.notice: A rise in broad prices cuts what a fixed amount of cash can buy.

noticeClaim.text: A rise in broad prices cuts the buying power of cash if its amount stays fixed.

fieldTry.title: Compounding
fieldTry.detail: Find one savings interest rate, and work out a year's interest on 1,000.
fieldTry.smaller: Find one savings interest rate.
cues: When I open my bank app
fieldTry.notice: Compound growth includes growth on past gains as well as on the starting amount.

noticeClaim.text: Compound growth includes growth on past gains as well as the starting amount.

fieldTry.title: The rule of 72
fieldTry.detail: Find one yearly interest rate in an ad, and divide 72 by it.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one yearly interest rate in an ad.
fieldTry.notice: The rule works for debt too: an unpaid card balance at 18% doubles in about four years.

noticeClaim.text: The rule works for debt too: an unpaid card balance at 18% interest doubles in about four years. One large Indian card issuer charges up to 3.75% a month, or 45% a year.

fieldTry.title: Risk and return
fieldTry.detail: Spot one ad that promises high returns, and look for its risk line.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one guaranteed-returns claim today.
fieldTry.notice: A high possible gain may mean more risk. The gain is not sure.

noticeClaim.text: A high possible gain may mean more risk. The gain is not sure.

fieldTry.title: Diversification
fieldTry.detail: Open one index fund's fact sheet and count the industries it holds.
fieldTry.smaller: Name 3 industries one fund invests in.
settings: A friend's fund, if they share it
fieldTry.notice: Four or five shares are not a real spread; a spread runs across many industries.

noticeClaim.text: Four or five shares are not a real spread. One investor guide asks for at least a dozen, across many industries.

fieldTry.title: What a stock is
fieldTry.detail: Pick one thing you used today and find the company that makes it.
fieldTry.smaller: Name the company behind one thing you used.
fieldTry.notice: A share gives part ownership of a company.

noticeClaim.text: A share gives part ownership of a company.

oldQuest.title: Sort a bill
oldQuest.detail: Name a planned bill and a surprise bill in a made-up hostel budget.

fieldTry.title: Emergency fund
fieldTry.detail: Look at one thing you use daily, and name a repair it could need without warning.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one possible repair for something you use.
fieldTry.notice: An emergency fund is cash kept for a sudden need.

noticeClaim.text: An emergency fund is cash kept for a sudden need.

oldQuest.title: Read a schedule
oldQuest.detail: In a sample EMI table, point to the principal, interest and balance columns.

fieldTry.title: EMI and loan cost
fieldTry.detail: Find one EMI offer and note the months and the total you would pay.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one EMI offer today.
fieldTry.notice: A longer loan term makes each EMI smaller but means paying more interest in total.

noticeClaim.text: A longer loan term makes each EMI smaller but means paying more interest in total.

oldQuest.title: Compare baskets
oldQuest.detail: Compare the holdings and fees in two made-up fund fact sheets.

fieldTry.title: Index funds and stock picking
fieldTry.detail: Find the expense ratio of one index fund and one active fund.
fieldTry.smaller: Find the expense ratio of one fund.
fieldTry.notice: Index funds trade little, so their expense ratios are lower than active funds'.

noticeClaim.text: Index funds follow a passive plan with little trading, so their expense ratios are lower than active funds.

oldQuest.title: Read the prompt
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up payment screen, identify the payer and the direction of money.

fieldTry.title: UPI scams and social engineering
fieldTry.detail: At a shop, spot one UPI QR stand, and recall: getting money needs no scan.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one shop QR stand; do not scan it.
fieldTry.notice: RBI says getting money never needs a QR scan or a PIN.

noticeClaim.text: RBI says getting money never needs a QR scan or a PIN, so take care if asked for either.

oldQuest.title: Spot a cue
oldQuest.detail: Watch one harmless daily act. Name the cue, the act, and the good result that may help it recur.

fieldTry.title: Habits
fieldTry.detail: Watch one of your daily acts and name its cue, like a place or the act before.
fieldTry.smaller: Name the cue for brushing your teeth.
fieldTry.notice: Cues in a stable setting can bring back a learned action with little thought.

noticeClaim.text: Cues in a stable setting, like a place or an act just before, can bring back a learned action with little thought.

oldQuest.title: Frame a token
oldQuest.detail: Write a made-up choice as a gain and then as a loss from a starting point. Ask how the frame may shift its feel.

fieldTry.title: Loss aversion
fieldTry.detail: Spot one line worded as a loss, like 'Don't miss out', and say it as a gain.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one 'Don't miss out' line today.
fieldTry.notice: A loss tends to weigh more than a gain of the same size.

noticeClaim.text: A loss tends to weigh more than a gain of the same size, so most people turn down a fair 50-50 chance to win or lose the same amount, more so as the stake grows.

oldQuest.title: Compare tags
oldQuest.detail: Pick two made-up price tags. Start a guess from each, then see how the first number may pull the guess.

fieldTry.title: Anchoring
fieldTry.detail: Spot one 'was this, now that' price, and ask what the first number does.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one crossed-out price today.
fieldTry.notice: A first number can pull a later estimate toward it, because people adjust away from it too little.

noticeClaim.text: A first number can pull a later estimate toward it, because people adjust away from it too little.

oldQuest.title: Try to disprove
oldQuest.detail: Pick a low-stakes belief about a game or bus. Write one clue that could show it is wrong.

fieldTry.title: Confirmation bias
fieldTry.detail: Pick one small belief, like your fastest route, and look for a clue against it.
fieldTry.smaller: Name one clue that could prove a small belief wrong.
cues: On my way to class or work
fieldTry.notice: A rule is tested properly by checking the cases that could prove it false.

noticeClaim.text: A rule of the form 'if p then q' is tested properly by checking the cases that could prove it false.

oldQuest.title: Watch a group cue
oldQuest.detail: In a harmless choice, note whether a visible group choice changes a guess. Keep the check kind.

fieldTry.title: Social proof
fieldTry.detail: Spot one crowd cue, like '10k bought this', and ask if it is proof.
fieldTry.smaller: Spot one bestseller tag today.
fieldTry.notice: A group can agree on a wrong answer, so agreement alone is a clue, not proof.

noticeClaim.text: A group can agree on a wrong answer, so agreement alone is a clue, not proof.

oldQuest.title: Time a small task
oldQuest.detail: Before a small school task, note a time guess. Afterward, note the time and one step the guess missed.

fieldTry.title: The planning fallacy
fieldTry.detail: Before one small task today, guess the minutes; after, note the real time.
fieldTry.smaller: Guess your travel time today, then check it.
fieldTry.notice: In one study, linking past tasks to a new plan removed the too-short bias.

noticeClaim.text: In one study, asking people to link past tasks to a new plan removed the too-short bias.

oldQuest.title: Trace a lesson
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up study day, mark learning first and later memory processing.

fieldTry.title: Sleep and memory
fieldTry.detail: After you study something today, sit quietly for 5 minutes before the next thing.
fieldTry.smaller: Sit quietly for 2 minutes after one lesson.
fieldTry.notice: A brief spell of quiet rest after learning helped memory more than spending that time on other tasks.

noticeClaim.text: A brief spell of quiet rest while awake after learning helped memory more than spending that time on other tasks.

oldQuest.title: Spot a pattern
oldQuest.detail: Compare a made-up fixed reward sequence with an uneven one.

fieldTry.title: Variable rewards
fieldTry.detail: Count how many times you check one app before noon. There is no target.
fieldTry.smaller: Notice one check that found nothing new.
fieldTry.notice: On a variable schedule, you cannot tell which try will bring the reward.

noticeClaim.text: On a variable schedule, the number of tries needed for a reward keeps changing, so you cannot tell which try will bring it.

oldQuest.title: Find the cue
oldQuest.detail: Mark the if part and then part in a made-up study plan.

fieldTry.title: If-then plans
fieldTry.detail: Pick one small task you already plan today, name its cue, then do it then.
fieldTry.smaller: Say one if-then plan out loud, then do it.
settings: For a call you keep putting off
fieldTry.notice: An if-then plan spells out the when, where and how in advance.

noticeClaim.text: An if-then plan spells out the when, where and how in advance: if situation Y comes, then I will do X.

oldQuest.title: Compare two views
oldQuest.detail: In a made-up class scene, compare the speaker’s guess with observers’ recall.

fieldTry.title: The spotlight effect
fieldTry.detail: Today, notice if anyone mentions your shirt's colour without being asked.
fieldTry.smaller: Name your shirt's colour to yourself, then see who notices.
fieldTry.notice: People wearing a striking T-shirt guessed that more people could recall it than really could.

noticeClaim.text: In two studies, people wearing a T-shirt with a striking image guessed that more people could recall it than really could.
